Protein Domain Retention of Isoforms

Source: R/productivity-evidence.R
domain_retention.Rd

Compares the Pfam domains of every isoform with those of the canonical isoform of its gene, using the APPRIS SPADE domain coordinates (frozen dataset appris_domains, frozen_data). For isoforms present in APPRIS the domain sets are compared directly. For other isoforms (novel transcripts) the genomic span of each canonical domain is projected onto the isoform: a domain is retained when the isoform covers the same exonic bases over the domain span and its ORF (see transcript_orfs(), or the annotated CDS) extends over it without a frameshift, partial when only part of the span is covered, and lost otherwise.

An altered_productive isoform that keeps all domains of the canonical protein is a milder event than one that loses a domain; the domain_retention_fraction column grades this and is included in transcript_productivity() output when the dataset is available.

Usage

domain_retention(self, gene_name = NULL, domains = NULL, ...)

Arguments

self

An IsoformicExperiment.

gene_name

Optional genes (names or IDs) to restrict the result to.

domains

Data frame or Parquet path of the domain table; NULL fetches the frozen appris_domains dataset.

...

Passed on to methods.

Value

A tibble with one row per transcript: n_domains_canonical, n_retained, n_partial, n_lost, domains_lost (Pfam names) and domain_retention_fraction (NA when the canonical isoform has no domain).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
iso <- example_isoformic()
domain_retention(iso, gene_name = "RBPJ")
} # }
